context:
Pick taken by the orchestrator, Oct 28 07:45 CDT, without your answer: (a), one writer only. It follows your later ruling for c136 (Oct 27 12:15 CDT) that sessions never write the page; sessions send their state to the writer, option (a), already on main. o8's option (c) is dropped and its lane ends with no code. Reversible: say so and (c) comes back.

Was asked: two of your rulings conflicted. o8, Oct 26: each session writes its own line after the local-write measure. c136, Oct 27 12:15 CDT: sessions never write the page; one writer does.
holds: The o8 lane (session lines on the roadmap page) is paused until you answer.

options.how: Sessions send their state to the writer, which publishes it. This is option (a), already built.
options.label: One writer only; drop (c)
options.lose: A session's state shows only once the writer publishes again.

options.how: Each session writes only its own unranked live/<session id> record; the writer keeps the items and their order.
options.label: Keep (c) as a narrow exception
options.lose: A second writer to the database; the Windows cost is unmeasured.

ref: o8 (a living roadmap page per repo), c136 (one page, one writer)
title: May each session write its own live line on the roadmap page, or does only the writer write it?
why: It keeps c136's one-writer rule with nothing new to build; the only cost is a short delay before a session's line shows.
